pr_body:
Continuation of https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/585

Added checks in both `onSendEnd` and `handleError`, fixes #371
pr_comments: @mcollina Any pointers as to where I can hook into the exception being thrown by fastify?
Oh, I will just write a test and see if it does not crash.

@mcollina I added a simple crash test, though I totally didn't expect the tests to pass on AppVeyor since I'm reading from `/dev/random`. Should I still polyfill it?

I've tested that it does indeed throw a non-zero exit code by locally reverting my fix.

I don't think the checks should be in `onSendEnd`. Headers should not have been sent yet when that function is called, so avoiding setting headers there could hide bugs (whereas throwing would help you know there's a problem).
I was wondering about that but I hadn't dug deep enough to verify that myself, was waiting for someone who's more familiar to point that out :)
I think we need this check everywhere headers can be manipulated because inside a middleware you have access to the raw response and it can change the headers before.

This solves a specific bug. Let’s treat things one at a time. If you are calling .writeHead() or manipulating the stream directly you are going against most of the fastify assumpions anyway. We are just not providing good feedback.

I've simplified the test case, tap automatically fails the test so I didn't have to listen for `uncaughtException` :)

I've also moved it to `test/stream.test.js` since I feel like it belongs there.

Updated the readable to return some random bytes, though I'm not quite sure what the deal is with Appveyor — perhaps a race condition triggering https://github.com/tapjs/node-tap/issues/345#issuecomment-279297584 🤔

The test is going to an endless loop in AppVeyor, it's spinning wheels for 30s without sending out any output:

```
not ok 36 - test/stream.test.js # time=30006.733ms
```
Closed in favor of https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/622. I'm sorry, but I would like to get this out asap.
This pull request has been automatically locked since there has not been any recent activity after it was closed. Please open a new issue for related bugs.

issue_context.title: streaming response + client closed connection is treated as an error
issue_context.body:
Server side code:
```
res.code(200).send(stream)
```

Client side is the `ffprobe` program from FFMpeg

```
$ ffprobe http://server:port/path/to/file
```

It seems to crash fastify because `ffprobe` closes connection once it knows enough about the file.

Fastify versions:
```
    "fastify": "^0.30.2",
    "fastify-auth": "^0.1.0",
    "fastify-helmet": "^1.0.1",
    "fastify-jwt": "^0.1.0",
    "fastify-multipart": "^0.2.0",
```

Console output:
```
06:44:49 🚨  client error
06:44:49 🚨  premature close
Error: Can't set headers after they are sent.
    at validateHeader (_http_outgoing.js:489:11)
    at ServerResponse.setHeader (_http_outgoing.js:496:3)
    at Immediate.wrapReplyEnd (node_modules/fastify/lib/reply.js:145:15)
    at runCallback (timers.js:789:20)
    at tryOnImmediate (timers.js:747:5)
    at processImmediate [as _immediateCallback] (timers.js:718:5)
[nodemon] app crashed - waiting for file changes before starting...
```
comments: Can you please upload an example to demonstrate your problem? (ideally without ffmpeg).
Closing this, if you have more questions feel free to reopen :)

I vaguely remember a mention around the time of the release of the current LTS a note about client hang-ups being handled in core differently. But I can't find the release note I'm thinking of to research it. My suspicion is that this is something in core, not Fastify (or emission from core that Fastify needs to handle).

@jsumners It might have been exclusive to the http2 module?

So far I've been able to reproduce it on the latest 6.x.x, 8.x.x and 9.x.x releases

review_comments: this is likely to trigger something close to an endless loop. Can you just push a value once, and not for every call to `read`? This might fix AppVeyor.
